courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Elementary Spanish I
courses.description: Introduction to listening, speaking, reading, and writing in Spanish and to the culture of Spanish-speaking regions.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Elementary Spanish II
courses.description: Continued listening, speaking, reading, and writing in Spanish with further study of the culture of Spanish-speaking regions.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Intermediate Spanish I
courses.description: A rapid review of grammar with continued use of listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in Spanish, all with a cultural emphasis.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Intermediate Spanish II
courses.description: This course focuses on listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in Spanish in an introduction to literature and within a cultural context.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: A Practical Application of Spanish Grammar
courses.description: A review of important structures of Spanish, presented in communicative contexts vital to the academic careers of students. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Introduction to Reading Hispanic Literature
courses.description: This course bridges language study and the study of literature by helping students read, understand, and interpret literature as a system of communication in Spanish.

restrictions.heading: Must be enrolled in one of the following Campuses

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish for Business I: Fundamentals
courses.description: Introduction to business language in the Hispanic world. Development of linguistic abilities to this end, with emphasis on those cultural factors that lead to commercial success. Conducted in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Medical Spanish
courses.description: This course facilitates acquisition of a broad vocabulary and awareness of cultural customs and trends pertaining to the healthcare field. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Latin American Music
courses.description: Students study the musical traditions of the Andes, Mexico and the Caribbean, focusing on the rhythms, instruments, artists, style and tendencies present. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Conversation: Issues and Strategies I
courses.description: Development of communicative ability and cross-cultural awareness through discussion of contemporary issues in the Hispanic world. Conducted in Spanish. No native speakers allowed.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Composition: Analysis and Development I
courses.description: Writings from the Hispanic world used as a springboard for analysis and enrichment of self-expression and development of precision in written communication. Incorporates grammar review. Conducted in Spanish. No native speakers allowed.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Cultural History of Spain II: Nineteenth and Twentieth Century Spain
courses.description: History of Spanish culture from 1800 to the present. Conducted in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Conversation Practicum
courses.description: This course combines current event discussion with ongoing conversation practice. Students participate in in-class discussions plus weekly language exchanges with native Spaniards. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Globalization in Latin America
courses.description: Case-studies examination of globalization in Latin America regarding politics and industry, migration, culture and communication, and health and the environment. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spain Today
courses.description: This course introduces students to current issues in the culture and history of contemporary Spain. Articles, videos, and news clips are used as springboard for discussion. Conducted in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Latin America Today
courses.description: Selected journalistic and literary writings used as a springboard for discussion of social, economic, and political issues of contemporary Latin America. Conducted in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Society in Hispanic Literature
courses.description: Study of Hispanic society and political thought in selected literary works. Conducted in Spanish.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level SPAN 2002 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish in Society: Authentic Cultural Narratives
courses.description: This course offers an interdisciplinary analysis of the language, culture, history and politics of select Spanish novels and/or television series. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Identity in Hispanic American Literature
courses.description: This course examines the construction of personal, cultural, national, political, and regional identity in Hispanic American literature over the past two centuries. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Satire & Media in the Americas
courses.description: This course explores how new types pf satire challenge traditional media and impacts political communication in today's democratic societies in the Americas. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Science Fiction in Latin America
courses.description: This course is a survey of Latin America science-fiction. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Issues of Sustainable Development in the Andean Region
courses.description: Historical and social context of contemporary issues of cultural, economic and environmental sustainability in the Andean region. Taught in Spanish.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level SPAN 2002 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Cultural Patrimony in Peru
courses.description: Using literature, film and art, this course examines cultural patrimony in Peru and its impact on society, economy, environment and threats to its preservation. Conducted in Spanish.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level SPAN 2002 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Culture and Commerce in the Andes
courses.description: Examines the 'business of nature' in the extractive economies of the Andes and culture clashes of Western and indigenous perspectives of development. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Commerce and Sustainable Communities
courses.description: Study of the connectedness and community impact of contemporary issues of economic, sociocultural, and environmental sustainability in Mexico. Conducted in Spanish. Part of the Spanish intensive summer LBAT program. Admission by application only.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Business and Culture in the Hispanic World
courses.description: Study of cultural issues, tendencies, and traditional patterns of behavior in Spanish-speaking people as they relate to business practices. Value systems and formal manifestations. Regional variations, including the U.S. Hispanic culture. Part of the Spanish intensive summer language program. Admission by application only.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level SPAN 1002 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level SPAN 1102 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Science and Technology in the Hispanic World
courses.description: Study of business organizations and use of technology in the Spanish-speaking world. Specialized vocabularies of business, economics, statistics, and computer science. Geographical and anthropological background.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Business and Culture in the Hispanic World: Seminar Abroad
courses.description: Field study of technology, economic trends, business firms, financial institutions, and cultural protocols in the Spanish-speaking area. Part of the Spanish intensive summer language program. Admission by application only.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish for Health Care Professionals
courses.description: Culture-specific conceptions of health, medical vocabulary, professional-patient protocols, professional-professional protocols, symptoms, treatments. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Health Care Industry in Spain
courses.description: Study of culture-specific values in health systems in Spain/ Europe. Visits to local sites. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Introduction to Caribbean Culture
courses.description: An introduction to the rich cultures of the Hispanic Caribbean islands (Cuba, Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico) and their diasporas in the US. Taught in Spanish.

restrictions.heading: Must be enrolled in one of the following Campuses

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Topics of current interest in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish for Science and Technology I: Fundamentals
courses.description: Introduction to scientific vocabulary and discourse in Spanish, by fields of interest. Study of expository texts, numerical expressions, and graphic aids. Development of some reading and translation strategies. Writing feature descriptions and article/report summaries in Spanish. Conducted in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish for Science and Technology II: Applications
courses.description: Advanced analysis of scientific and technological discourse in Spanish. Focus on reading strategies and oral discussion of topics such as use and transfer of technology and the acculturation issues that follow. Further development of comprehension, production, and translation strategies, with emphasis on professional communications and on writing feature descriptions, summaries, and abstracts. Conducted in Spanish.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level SPAN 3062 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish for the Professions
courses.description: This course develops communication skills for professional purposes with an emphasis on specialized vocabulary building and cultural nuances of the Spanish-speaking world. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Learning in the Hispanic Community
courses.description: This class combines classroom discussion with Hispanic community service projects to allow students to study Hispanic cultures and practice Spanish with native speakers. Conducted in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Service-Learning Abroad I
courses.description: Students complete service projects in a Spanish-speaking country abroad and attend weekly class meetings that combine student presentations and documentaries with a guest-speaker series. Conducted in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Service-Learning Abroad II
courses.description: Students complete service projects in a Spanish-speaking country abroad and gain an in-country immersion opportunity that hones oral and aural skills and increases cultural competence through real-life interactions with the host community abroad. Conducted in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Social, Cultural, and Linguistic Diversity in Spain
courses.description: This course examines the social, cultural, and linguistic dimensions of sustainability and the concepts of diversity and equity in the Spanish context. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: U.S. Spanish: Language and Cultures
courses.description: Linguistic groups, changes, bilingualism, customs, traditions of US Hispanics. Course project on current migration, legal, financial, educational, health, media or political issues/advances. Conducted in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Bilingualism in the Spanish Speaking World
courses.description: This course introduces students to bilingualism at both individual and societal levels within the Hispanic communities in the US, Spain, and Latin America. Conducted in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Applied Linguistics
courses.description: Advanced linguistic analysis of the Spanish language, particularly as it contrasts with English. Conducted in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Nation and Narration in Latin America
courses.description: This course examines the connection between nation and narration in Latin American literature and film and explores the narrative construction of national identities. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Food, Power, and Sustainability in Latin America
courses.description: Food as gateway to region-by-region study of issues of sustainable development in Latin America. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Visual Culture and Social Agenda in Latin America
courses.description: Historical and cultural analysis of the role of art, visual image and iconography as social commentator and public platform in Latin America. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Hispanic Community Internship
courses.description: Students complete inernships with agencies, organizations, and businesses serving Atlanta Hispanics, using their Spanish language skills in a professional work environment. Conducted in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Span Sociolinguistics
courses.description: This course explores the relationships between the Spanish language and the Hispanic cultures and societies of the world. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Ibero-American Cities
courses.description: This course examines the representation and development of cities in the Hispanic World. Students develop three urban projects based on their study. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Covering Arts & Latin(o) American Culture in the U.S
courses.description: This course explores contemporary media reporting on the LatinX culture in the US and Latin America. Taught in Spanish and English.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Globalization and Migration
courses.description: Print and filmic texts serve as gateway to context-specific issues of migration in the Spanish-speaking world from both sender- and receiver-country perspectives. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Latin American Documentaries
courses.description: This course explores the documentary traditions of Chile, Argentina and Cuba to learn about the history of Latin American societies. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Media and Power in Latin America
courses.description: This course explores the tensions between media and power in relation to the struggle for freedom of expression in Latin American countries. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Latin America through Film
courses.description: Contemporary Latin American film serves as gateway to in-depth discussion of social, political, economic and cross-cultural perspectives. Conducted in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Hispanic Digital Cultures
courses.description: Students explore recent developments in New Media and Digital Culture within the context of Latin American and Spanish cultures and societies. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Advanced Intercultural Seminar
courses.description: Integrates cross-cultural research and reflection into discussion of current issues in the Hispanic world. Intended for students who have had some study abroad experience in a Spanish-speaking country. Conducted in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Intercultural Dialogue
courses.description: Explores cultural identity in Latin America through live interviews, print, and film. Topics will vary. Taught in Spanish as part of the LBAT study abroad program.
